results.snippet:
This guide explains how to use OAuth access tokens to authenticate API requests to Zendesk. It covers the two supported OAuth flows, how to implement token refresh, and security best practices.
OAuth is the recommended authentication method because it:
- Doesn’t require users to share their personal API token with your integration
- Is tied to a user account, so tokens inherit that user's permissions and can't be used to access resources beyond what the authorizing user can access
- Supports fine-grained permissions through scopes, so you can limit a token to only the access your integration actually needs
- Uses short-lived tokens that expire automatically, reducing the risk if a token is compromised
- Is optimal for long-term app security and maintenance
## How OAuth authentication works
Instead of sending a static API token with every request, your integration obtains an OAuth access token and includes that in the request header. Access tokens are short-lived and paired with a refresh token that your integration uses to automatically get a new access token when the current one expires.

results.title: How can I authenticate API requests?
results.snippet:
You must be a [verified user](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408886752410-Verifying-an-end-user-s-email-address) to make authenticated API requests. To authenticate API requests, use basic authentication with your email address and password, your email address and an API token, or an OAuth access token.

## API token authentication
If you use an [API token](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408889192858-Generating-a-new-API-token), combine your email address and API token to generate the authorization header. Format the email address and API token combination as a `Base-64` encoded string. For an example of how to format the authorization header, see the code block below.
```auto
Authorization: Basic {base-64-encoded email_address/token:api_token}
```
## OAuth access token authentication
If you use OAuth to authenticate, format the authorization header this way:
```auto
Authorization: Bearer oauth_access_token
```
For more information, see [Using OAuth authentication with your application](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408845965210-Using-OAuth-authentication-with-your-application).

You can also create OAuth access tokens on your own behalf without building an authorization flow. If you already have a valid OAuth access token, you can use the API to create additional access tokens. If you don't have one yet, see [Getting your first token](/documentation/authentication/oauth-migration/#getting-your-first-token) for one-time browser setup instructions to get your first token.
This guide shows how you can use the API to create OAuth access tokens on your own behalf. The guide also covers how to use OAuth access tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests.
## Creating an OAuth client
To create an access token, you need an OAuth client. You can use the same OAuth client to create multiple access tokens.
You can create an OAuth client in one of two ways:

results.title: Migrating from API tokens to OAuth access tokens
results.snippet:
# Migrating from API tokens to OAuth access tokens
Zendesk API tokens will be permanently deactivated on April 30, 2027. If your integration, script, or app currently uses an API token to call a Zendesk API, you need to migrate to OAuth before that date.
This guide shows you how to:
- Choose the right OAuth flow
- Get your first OAuth credentials
- Keep your integration working automatically when tokens expire

API tokens have limitations that make them a poor fit for long-term use:
- **No expiry**: If a token is compromised, it stays valid until it's manually deactivated.
- **No scope restrictions**: A token can access any endpoint the authenticating user is allowed to use.
- **No application binding**: Any system that has the token and its associated email address can use it.
## Migration timeline
Zendesk is retiring Support API tokens in three phases between July 2026 and April 2027.

|---|---|
| July 28, 2026 | **Phase 1: Auto-deactivation begins.** On July 28, 2026, these updates take effect: - Any API token that hasn't been used for 30 days will be automatically deactivated. Deactivated tokens can't be used to make API requests. - If a deactivated token

results.title: Chat Conversations API
results.snippet:
The reference documentation for the Conversations API is available at [https://zendesk.github.io/conversations-api/](https://zendesk.github.io/conversations-api/).
The Conversations API is the first GraphQL API released by Zendesk. The docs are hosted on a separate site to take advantage of the GraphQL schema. One benefit of using GraphQL is that high-quality API documentation can be generated directly from the GraphQL schema.

### API path
The Conversations API uses one of the following paths:
**WebSocket**
`wss://chat-api.zopim.com/stream/0.1/graphql/{session_id}:{client_id}`
**HTTP**
`POST https://chat-api.zopim.com/graphql/request`
Use HTTP for authentication. Make all other requests through a WebSocket connection.
The Chat REST API is unaffected by the introduction of the new path for the Conversations API.

results.title: GraphQL
results.snippet:
# GraphQL
Search API provides [GraphQL](http://graphql.org) query API, currently for companies only. It has no filtering or sorting capabilities, but it is a convenient way of exploring company hierarchies.
GraphQL companies query takes a list of company IDs as an argument and set of projections to apply on companies with those IDs. Projections may include all regular company attributes, but in GraphQL company has fields describing relations within company hierarchy, that can also be queried. Relations are defined as connections in [Relay format](https://facebook.github.io/relay/docs/en/graphql-in-relay.html).
Currently, query nesting is limited to one level (e.g. one can query children and ancestors for given company, but not children's children or ancestors' roots), with following exceptions:
- Query parent for ancestor:
```
{ companies(ids: [1]) {   ancestors {     edges {       node {         id         parent {           edges {             node {               id             }           }         }       }     }   } }}
```
- Query children count for some relation
```
{ companies(ids: [2]) {   children {     edges {       node {         children {           count         }

results.title: Search
results.snippet:
The Search API is a unified search API that returns tickets, users, and organizations. You can define filters to narrow your search results according to resource type, dates, and object properties, such as ticket requester or tag.

To use the API with Python or Node.js, see [Searching with the Zendesk API](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/searching-with-the-zendesk-api).

### Query syntax
The search endpoint has a `query` parameter:
`.../api/v2/search?query={search_string}`
The `query` parameter value supports a syntax that lets you specify resource types and criteria. For example, you can search for "users named Jane Doe" or "tickets with an open status".
For more information about the query syntax and examples, see [Searching with the Zendesk API](/documentation/ticketing/using-the-zendesk-api/searching-with-the-zendesk-api).

### List Search Results
- `GET /api/v2/search?query={query}`
Returns the search results. See Query syntax for details on the `query` parameter.
Use the ampersand character (&) to append the `sort_by` or `sort_order` parameters to the URL.

results.title: Unlocking new possibilities: Revolutionizing service with the Zendesk AI MCP client
results.snippet:
At Zendesk, our mission is to enhance customer experiences with smarter, easier, more adaptable AI solutions. That’s why we’re bringing Model Context Protocol (MCP) into the Zendesk Resolution Platform. MCP’s open-source model offers a simple, standardized path towards integrating AI with business data. With MCP, Zendesk’s AI Agents and Copilots get the relevant, real-time data they need to go beyond isolated language models, improve AI accuracy, and drive better outcomes for agents and customers.
### What is a Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
AI assistants can connect to external tools with APIs, but this often requires custom, one-off integrations with limited extensibility and scalability. The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol), changes this. It’s a standard, open framework that gives AI assistants a simple, unified way to access and interact with external data.

results.title: Announcing the general availability of the MCP client
results.snippet:
Zendesk is excited to announce the general availability of the MCP client, which makes it possible to use the tools on an MCP server in action flows to fetch data and take actions in external systems.

With this release, admins can connect their Zendesk account to MCP (model context protocol) servers. Both public MCP servers from vendors such as Asana, Stripe, or Github, and private MCP servers are supported.
When you connect Zendesk to an MCP server, the MCP client finds all of the tools the MCP server has and lets you choose which ones you want to expose for use in action flows. When used in action flows, the MCP server tools can be used by AI-powered features, such as [auto assist](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/7051314237466), [AI agents](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/8966284087066), and [custom agents (EAP)](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10724438136858), streamlining how you fetch data from and perform actions in external systems and expanding what you can do with Zendesk in your business workflows.

results.title: MCP Client Connector integration with Zendesk
results.snippet:
# MCP Client
## Zendesk’s MCP Client allows you to easily connect your Zendesk instance to external MCP Servers.
### About this connector
OAuth-based connections
Our MCP Client takes care of Dynamic Client Registration, kicking off the OAuth flow, securely storing auth credentials, and securely using OAuth tokens to authenticate tool calls. For MCP Servers that require it, we also provide the ability to manually enter OAuth client details.
Tool discovery
Once connected the server’s MCP tools are discovered and processed to capture the tool names, descriptions, input fields, and (if provided by the server) output fields.
Tool management
Your Admins can select which tools they want to make available to Zendesk AI Agents and Action Flows.
Use tools in Action Flows
Tools are made available as steps to use in Action Flows, easily adding new third-party functionality to event-driven workflows, and AI use cases like Auto Assist, AI Agents, and Custom Agents.

MCP Client is available to use on any Zendesk Suite or Zendesk Support plan.
### How to connect
In Admin Center, go to Apps and integrations > Connections > Connections
